title: HDI Global posts 90.3% combined ratio as specialty rates keep sliding
full_text:
Corporate and specialty insurer HDI Global SE posted a combined ratio of 90.3% for the first nine months of 2026, an improvement on the 91.6% recorded over the same period a year earlier, according to the company’s nine-month results. Operating profit rose 6% to €584 million, while its contribution to Talanx Group net income climbed 11% to €455 million.
At 90.3%, HDI is absorbing claims and expenses at well below the break-even threshold of 100%, leaving a meaningful technical margin at a point in the cycle when that margin is under pressure across the market. The insurance service result, a broader measure of underwriting profitability under IFRS 17, rose 15% to €733 million from €638 million.
Revenue came in at €7.6 billion, unchanged year-on-year. HDI attributed the stability to disciplined new business underwriting rather than market or demand factors. Chief executive officer Edgar Puls (pictured) framed it as a deliberate posture. “Our full focus remains on active cycle management and a prudent, long-term approach to risk selection and pricing,” he said. “This enables us to protect the quality and profitability of our portfolio while continuing to provide our clients and broker partners with the expertise and reliability they need.”
According to WTW’s Specialty Insurance Marketplace Survey published in October 2026, approximately 65% of the cumulative rate gains built up across specialty lines between 2017 and the market peak in 2023 had unwound by the July 2026 renewals, with every one of the 15 tracked classes recording a net-of-claims-trend rate decrease in the first half of the year. For brokers placing complex risks in that environment, an insurer’s combined ratio provides a more reliable read of financial sustainability than its top-line growth.
HDI’s nine-month performance lands seven weeks before a significant structural change to its distribution. Syndicate 2029, which received Lloyd’s permission to underwrite on November 10, opens for business on January 1, 2027. The syndicate will write 13 lines from day one, covering credit and political risk, cyber, political violence and terrorism, financial and professional lines, fine art and specie, marine cargo, medical malpractice, clinical trials and bloodstock. It gives brokers a Lloyd’s market route to HDI capacity that has not previously existed.
The syndicate forms part of HDI’s Xcelerate29 strategy, the four-year growth plan launched in February 2026 targeting selective international expansion and underwriting excellence through to 2029. Puls said the nine-month results reflected the work of the company’s employees in bringing that strategy to life.
HDI Global is part of the Talanx Group and carries a financial strength rating of AA-/stable from Standard & Poor’s and A+/stable from AM Best, according to the company.
